info.title: Interceptor API for Operator
info.description: Operator-facing API only. Administrative CLI commands and Interceptor-only configuration are excluded. Before attachment consumers require exact agreement with their independently reviewed contract version and complete-document SHA-256 pins. Source commits and product versions are not compatibility pins. All schema references are included in this document.

servers.description: Existing trusted-host loopback API. Campaign identifiers scope access; they do not authenticate hostile local processes.

post.description: Read-only, no campaign or target access, no runtime reconciliation; Cache-Control: no-store Operator compares both the returned version and document SHA-256 with its independently pinned supported version and hash before attachment; mismatch or unreadable identity stops campaign execution The hash identifies the contract document, not an executable, release archive, capability manifest, API response or canonicalized subset; its value is not embedded in the document itself Both version and exact document hash must match, including after formatting-only edits; pins are never learned from the running service; no source-commit pin, Internet lookup or user-supplied document is required

200.description: Evidence tar archive, potentially containing explicitly partial evidence. Verify transfer integrity, member schemas, native hashes, identity bindings and completeness before accepting any outcome.

x-evidence-members.condition: Required for complete final evaluation; absence makes the bundle partial.
Required when session.parent_session_id is set; verify the source chain and checkpoint prefix independently.
Every referenced blob from events, both journals, the file manifest and artifact registries, including unchanged and empty seed files.

x-evidence-integrity.archive: Only regular tar members with unique clean relative paths; no traversal, links or extraction needed. Check Content-Length and X-Content-SHA256 against received bytes and enforce negotiated/local capacity. A valid tar checksum or HTTP 200 alone is not provenance verification.
x-evidence-integrity.native_json: Hash UTF-8 encoding/json.Marshal output with the designated hash/digest field set to the empty string (not removed), no indentation or final newline. x-native-json-order gives struct member order; x-native-json-omitempty gives Go empty-value omission rules. Struct values (including zero attribution) are not empty; nil slices/maps encode null unless omitted; empty nonnil slices/maps encode []/{}. Map keys sort lexically; raw JSON retains member order while whitespace is compacted. Preserve Go HTML escaping (<, >, &, U+2028/U+2029), timestamp encoding, and exact integer values. These are not JCS or hashes of pretty-printed archive members. Unknown fields or unsupported schemas fail verification.
x-evidence-integrity.chains: Verify event and transaction SHA-256 chains from sha256: plus 64 zeroes, contiguous sequences starting at 1, and matching session identities. Include every operation and owner field. Check checkpoint hash, source session, journal sequence/hash, file manifest digest and restore lineage. Source journal prefixes must remain independently verifiable.
x-evidence-integrity.files: Require supported manifest schema, sorted unique clean absolute paths, valid types and permission bits. Schema 2 requires owner=application or supervisor on every entry; schema 1 forbids ownership and remains historical evidence only. Do not infer portable numeric UID/GID. Ownership-aware filesystem writes carry owner; absence in historical records is not authorization to restore them. Validate each file/database/artifact blob digest and recorded size.
x-evidence-integrity.bindings: Cross-check campaign, session, environment, application and capability identities across metadata, bundle, checkpoints, registries and execution records. Verify the execution-state digest committed in the journal and the EvidenceBundle digest. Product/source provenance is not an Operator compatibility pin.
x-evidence-integrity.completeness: Respect partial/truncated and failure markers, evaluation availability, coverage gaps and unknown operations. Oracle verdicts and application-authored assertions do not override failed provenance. Complete evidence means a complete record, not a successful attack.

adaptive.CapabilityManifest.description: Schema of the separate build-generated manifest returned by the API. Values and availability are environment-specific, not enumerated by this contract.

value.description: Application-defined JSON value; interpreted according to the selected delivery or observation kind.

adaptive.OperationRecord.description: A successful operation.status lookup returns HTTP 200 even while the recorded operation is running. Only running records may contain the exact unassigned response {status: 0, session_revision: 0}; completed and unknown records require a normal recorded response. This does not make 0 an HTTP status.

body_digest.description: SHA-256 with sha256: prefix over the exact serialized body JSON bytes; reserialization can change identity.

ContractSHA256.description: SHA-256 of every UTF-8 byte of this complete document, including formatting and final newline. Not canonicalized JSON or an artifact checksum. The actual digest is not embedded here.

native_response.description: Original JSON result retained when a deadline leaves the operation outcome uncertain.

ErrorBody.description: Errors may be direct body.code or a forwarded body.error object. Unknown codes are failures, never success. Outcome-unknown errors require operation.status reconciliation before retrying. Evidence-storage failures invalidate evidence-dependent outcomes.

SnapshotCreate.description: Omitted allowance uses native remaining capacity; zero means no allowance. Runtime budgets remain Interceptor-owned.

SessionOwnerRequest.description: Terminal campaign closure bypasses the mutation queue and revision race; already-dispatched work can finish and remains reportable No implicit target-stop permission, ownership transfer or reopening; healthy planned restore uses lifecycle instead of prior terminal closure

SessionStatusRequest.description: A missing record or failed lookup never establishes non-execution; running includes queued work Retained reporting uses preserved campaign association without restarting the target

OperationStatusRequest.description: A missing record or failed lookup never establishes non-execution; running includes queued work Retained reporting uses preserved campaign association without restarting the target

CapabilitiesReadRequest.description: Operator reads this manifest before selecting campaign actions; matching contract versions does not imply every target supports every action The manifest is a separate build-derived resource; target configuration and available values are not enumerated in this contract; runtime policy still governs admission

ArtifactRegisterRequest.description: Artifacts and attempts are scoped to the campaign and integrity-checked before dependent actions; registration does not authorize arbitrary target operations

ArtifactReadRequest.description: Artifacts and attempts are scoped to the campaign and integrity-checked before dependent actions; registration does not authorize arbitrary target operations

AttemptRegisterRequest.description: Artifacts and attempts are scoped to the campaign and integrity-checked before dependent actions; registration does not authorize arbitrary target operations

InjectionArmRequest.description: Deleting an injection does not undo previous effects; restored injections remain eligible for campaign-scoped cleanup Response alteration is distinct from persisted state alteration and does not prove committed target changes No service implementation inventory is implied; Operator selects actions using the environment manifest

InjectionDeleteRequest.description: Deleting an injection does not undo previous effects; restored injections remain eligible for campaign-scoped cleanup Response alteration is distinct from persisted state alteration and does not prove committed target changes No service implementation inventory is implied; Operator selects actions using the environment manifest

ApplicationInvokeRequest.description: Supervisor-observed activity is attributed to the active invocation window, never trusted from target-supplied attribution headers Runtime/provider configuration stays with Interceptor; this API does not select a model provider or alter application launch configuration

ObservationReadRequest.description: Feedback profiles filter disclosure; fixed receipts prevent widening the view with later reads Observed attribution describes the invocation window; outcome verdicts come from independent observations/oracles, not agent-authored claims

ObservationContentReadRequest.description: Feedback profiles filter disclosure; fixed receipts prevent widening the view with later reads Observed attribution describes the invocation window; outcome verdicts come from independent observations/oracles, not agent-authored claims

SnapshotCreateRequest.description: Availability comes from the environment manifest; application memory is restorable only through the declared state contract, not process-memory capture Caller byte allowance can only tighten native limits; zero is exhausted; failed or oversized snapshots are not committed Creation, retained metadata lookup and lifecycle restoration are separate API operations

NativeRequest.description: Select by request.operation. Each variant constrains its body. x-response-schema links that variant to its success response component; all variants may return ErrorResponse or InProgressResponse. No artificial HTTP routes are introduced.

PendingOperationResponse.description: Unassigned response stored in a running native operation record. It is not an HTTP response and is invalid outside that context. No body is present.

semantic.description: Event-kind-specific observation data, including application/service-defined content. Preserve it in hash verification; it is not a trusted application outcome by itself.

path.description: Clean absolute path; no dot segments. Entries are unique and sorted lexically by path.

snapshot.Manifest.description: New sessions emit schema 2 with logical application/supervisor ownership, including root directories. Schema 1 is readable historical evidence without ownership; never infer an owner. Legacy evidence readability does not imply native restore support. Digest covers ownership and permission bits. Missing/invalid ownership in schema 2 and unsupported versions are rejected.

value.description: JSON value; its kind-specific structure is defined by the containing record. Preserve member ordering when verifying native hashes.
Application/service-defined JSON resource, retained without losing JSON member ordering for native hashes.

statejournal.Operation.description: Discriminated journal operation. owner is permitted only for file_upsert, directory_ensure and symlink_set. Current ownership-aware writes include owner; historical writes may omit it. Omitted mode/size mean zero. Journal schema remains 1; file_manifest_schema in environment_materialized identifies ownership-aware state and is independent of transaction schema_version. Preserve owner in native hashing, never strip unknown fields to make verification succeed.

baseline_file_manifest_digest.description: Empty for an unmaterialized baseline, otherwise a sha256 digest.

EvidenceFailureMarker.description: Host diagnostic record. Presence marks partial evidence; fields are diagnostic and are not an execution authorization or a successful outcome.
